page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The complex with haemoglobin
lines: Haemoglobin is the substance in blood
that carries oxygen. It binds oxygen as
Carbon monoxide CO that is breathed in
binds to the same haemoglobin and forms
steps.why: Carbon monoxide is poisonous because of where it goes in the body, not because it burns or corrodes. It binds at the same site on haemoglobin that oxygen uses, so the first half of the answer is naming that complex.
common_mistakes: Writing that CO reacts with the oxygen in the lungs. It binds to haemoglobin, not to oxygen.
Naming CO₂ as the poisonous oxide. Carbon dioxide is not poisonous in this way; carbon monoxide is.
steps.memory_tip: Carbon monoxide goes to the same place oxygen goes — the haemoglobin.
steps.margin_note: Name haemoglobin and name both complexes, CO–Hb and O₂–Hb.

steps.label: Why oxygen is not carried

lines.text: CO–Hb is far more stable than O₂–Hb

lines: The CO–Hb complex is about 300 times
more stable than the O₂–Hb complex.
So the carbon monoxide stays attached
and that haemoglobin is no longer
The blood then supplies less oxygen to
the body, and this is why CO is
steps.why: The number is the reason. If the two complexes were of similar stability the carbon monoxide would come off again and do little damage. Because the CO complex is about 300 times more stable, the haemoglobin is taken out of use.
common_mistakes: Writing only that CO forms a complex. The answer needs the comparison: that complex is about 300 times more stable than the oxygen one.
Writing that CO destroys the haemoglobin. The haemoglobin is not destroyed; it is occupied by CO and cannot carry oxygen.
steps.memory_tip: About 300 times more stable — that one number is the whole reason CO is poisonous.
steps.margin_note: Give the figure of about 300 times and then state the result, that oxygen is no longer carried.

insider_note: Most students write that carbon monoxide forms a complex with haemoglobin and stop there. The comparison completes it: the CO complex is about 300 times more stable than the oxygen complex, and that is why the blood no longer carries oxygen.
